english: Ashes of Brigdarrow[PARAGRAPH]CHAPTER 1: DAIN[PARAGRAPH]The Illian village of Brigdarrow was enjoying one of the last warm days of autumn and Dain thought that weapons practice was a poor way to spend it. [PARAGRAPH]Thegn Garon Ire was leading a few of the village boys through horseman training, an opportunity Dain lost after unsuccessfully attempting to get one of the villages dappled gray tarpans to leap over a low fence. Garon claimed that the role of horseman was suited only to young men who took themselves more seriously, so Dain was left to be trained as a simple spearman. [PARAGRAPH]The only girl practicing in the villages open square was Kirien Birn. At thirteen she was a year younger than Dain and the only one more likely to get into trouble. But unlike Dain her disarming smile got her out of the trouble her mischievous nature got her into. Today she had her curly hair tied back as her mother led her through archery practice. [PARAGRAPH]Only men were able to directly fight and die for the village, as Kirien's father had almost six years ago. Kirien hated that she could only use a bow and frequently claimed she could best Dain in a spear fight, which was probably true. [PARAGRAPH]Dain was startled as a horse went thundering by with Caspian bouncing unsteadily atop it as Caspian navigated around the stone warhorse that formed the center of the village square and connected with a crash to the wooden shield set as a target for the boys practice. The resulting impact was a surprise to everyone, but most surprising to Caspian who went off the back of his horse, feet over his head, and slammed into the ground. The horse seemed almost as jarred by the hit and continued its run to the stable, where it slipped inside and returned to its stall. [PARAGRAPH]As Garon and others gathered around the fallen Caspian, Dain wandered to the squares edge. The village had no wall and the eastern side of the square was open to grasslands and fields. With a final glance to make sure no one was watching Dain sprinted away from the village and past the few chickens that were Brigdarrow's only active guards. [PARAGRAPH]They must have been worried about Caspian because no one noticed him leaving. No one yelled for Dain to return, not that he would have. The dull grinding boredom of the afternoon immediately slipped away as the thrill of freedom swept over him, pushing his legs even faster. Suddenly the air seemed crisper, the sun brighter and the world a boy's paradise. [PARAGRAPH]Dain slowed to a walk once he was safely away from Brigdarrow. He cut across the recently harvested fields of Ulvin Farm where small brown mice hunted for fallen grain. [PARAGRAPH]Past the farm Dain stopped to look at Tarch's Tower, a three story stone tower which appeared to have no door and a single window on its top floor. Earlier that summer Dain discovered the door to the tower, stairs led down to it at the towers base but the adults of Brigdarrow heaped enough dirt around the tower to bury it. Unable to reach the window, and noticing that rocks simply bounced off the glass, Dain dug down to the door and attempted to pick the doors triangular lock with a thin knife. Just as he inserted the knife he was struck with a blast like lightning. Dain awoke to find himself on his back nearly fifteen foot from the tower with one of his shoes knocked completely off. It was the most exciting event of his life. Still he hadn't been able to work up the courage to try it again. Not yet at least. [PARAGRAPH]Dain watched the tower window. Some of the village boys claimed they saw a figure pass by it, someone walking inside the tower. That and sightings of the monstrous Nuckelavee in the lake that bordered Brigdarrow were common sources of rumors for the village boys, but Dain had never seen either of them. [PARAGRAPH]A cloud rolled in front of the sun and Dain squinted to try to make out anything in the towers window. He was so intent on this that he didn't hear the grass rustling behind him. He heard running and spun, readying his spear, but he was too slow. The spear's length was jammed into his chest and the attacker's full weight fell on him, knocking him backwards. Dain's eyes were huge as he imagined one of the forests wild boars preparing to tear into his throat. [PARAGRAPH]Kirien started laughing uncontrollably. She sat on his stomach, her hands on his spear, holding it against him as she laughed so hard the spear shuddered. Determined not to look any more foolish Dain pushed her aside and sat up. She easily rolled off into the grass laughing. [PARAGRAPH]"You're lucky I didn't stab you, you could have been killed. " Dain said, trying to regain his composure. But it didn't help, she just laughed harder. [PARAGRAPH]It wasn't until he began to stomp away that she got up, taking deep breaths as her laughter subsided. She jogged up beside him, and when he glanced over he could see a whole afternoon of teasing in her smile and green eyes. But she decided to let the teasing go, for now. [PARAGRAPH]"Where are you going?" she asked. [PARAGRAPH]"Don't know, just exploring," Dain found it impossible to stay angry at her, although he fought to keep his look of indignation, "anything is better than spear practice. "[PARAGRAPH]"I don't know if you are going to get into more trouble for skipping out of practice, heading into the countryside alone or taking one of Garon's spears. "[PARAGRAPH]For the first time Dain noticed that he brought the spear with him. Garon said that if he practiced with it enough it would begin to feel like a natural extension of him. During his first few lessons the spear felt so heavy and unnatural he couldn't imagine that happening. Now he had been carrying it for over a quarter of an hour and he hadn't noticed it. [PARAGRAPH]Dain looked at his spear with a newfound respect. "If you are so worried why don't you head back and save yourself from the switch, or whatever they dream up for me this time. "[PARAGRAPH]"Nah, I'm not going to miss the fun. " Kirien untied the cord that was holding her hair back and let it fall around her face. She ran her hands through it, doing whatever girls do that makes their hair look essentially unchanged but Dain found the process somehow mesmerizing. She had freckles along her nose from the summer spent outside, and round cheeks that dimpled when she smiled. Kirien noticed Dain watching her and replied only with a slight smile that made him feel suddenly shy. [PARAGRAPH]"What are you worried about?" Dain asked, "Your mother isn't going to be nearly as mad as my dad. "[PARAGRAPH]Kirien started to argue but they both knew it was true. Kirien's mother, Jerra, and Dain's father, Havis, had very different ideas about discipline. Dain's mother had died giving birth to him, leaving Havis as a single parent. Since the goblin attack that killed Kirien's father, her mother raised her alone. It was obvious to the village that Jerra and Havis had become close. They spent much of their time together talking or helping each other with tasks, Jerra made all of Dain's clothes and Havis built the shelving in Jerra's small store. But among the Illian's marriage was forever and a widow would never consider a new relationship, so they remained only friends. [PARAGRAPH]Kirien and Dain talked about this as they walked. They both dreamed that their parents would someday take them to a wonderful city that didn't have such an inflexible view toward relationships. They had talked about these ideas for more than a year and at first it had been an uncomfortable subject because Kirien still loved and remembered her own father well, but over time she realized how much happier her mother was when spending time with Havis. [PARAGRAPH]Dain's story about running off to another city had veered completely out of the range of reality. He was talking about giant frogs they would ride to their mansion when Kirien stopped him by putting a hand clumsily in front of his mouth. Dain was surprised to be interrupted and was about to complain when he noticed her other hand, which pointed to a small copse of trees. [PARAGRAPH]Not more than sixty feet ahead a pair of huge beetles sat. Both beetles were large enough to replace the frogs in Dain's story. One lay contentedly at the edge of the tree's, enjoying the sun, digesting some recently eaten meal, or doing whatever giant bugs do when they sitting unmoving. If it wasn't for the other one Dain and Kirien might not have noticed them. It couldn't be more different from the first. It dug frantically at the base of one of the trees. Both bugs had huge enameled horns growing out of their foreheads and this beetle's horn occasionally caught on the tree, tearing deep grooves through the bark and wood underneath. [PARAGRAPH]"What do you suppose it's looking for?" Kirien whispered as she crouched in the grass. [PARAGRAPH]"I don't know, maybe it just really hates trees. " Then after a pause Dain added, "I guess there is only one way to find out. "[PARAGRAPH]Kirien looked skeptical, the accidental gouges in the tree showed that the beetles could cause considerable damage, even if they weren't particularly aggressive. But her curiosity got the best of her and she waited to see what Dain would do. [PARAGRAPH]Feeling the ground, eyes still focused on the beetles, Dain found a few decent sized rocks. Mustering his courage Dain jumped up and yelled at the beetles, running to within forty feet as he hurled the stones at them. His shout sounded sincere and his aim was good, most of the rocks struck the beetles. But they bounced harmlessly off of the bug's thick exoskeleton. Neither bug seemed to notice. [PARAGRAPH]Dain looked back to see that Kirien's green eyes were even wider than normal. She seemed impressed with his daring and her look, more than any real interest in the beetles, gave him the courage to continue on. Gripping his spear tightly Dain started walking toward the beetle. He circled so that another tree was between him and the burrowing beetle and crept up to within fifteen feet of the giant bug. At this distance if the beetle were to turn and lunge, if such a creature could lunge, Dain guessed he would still be out of reach of the beetles giant horn. [PARAGRAPH]The lounging beetle's black eyes glanced emotionlessly at Dain. Since it was further away Dain wasn't too concerned with that one. His interest was focused on the beetle that was still tearing and digging at the base of one of the copse's trees. By this point the tree looked close to toppling with each strike of the beetles horn. [PARAGRAPH]Dain crept so close that he was getting hit with the occasional clump of dirt the beetle threw into the air. Still the beetle was so fixated on its digging that it seemed oblivious to him. It was the moment most boys would turn back, that moment his father had long lectured him about, when you must do the right thing. But the lectures and his father were a world away to Dain right now. Summoning his courage he ran toward the beetle and leapt onto its wide back. [PARAGRAPH]For a second he stood triumphant on the powerful creature. Completely overwhelmed with the joy of the moment he didn't notice the beetles shaking attempt to dislodge him. Dain floundered at the sudden movement. Kirien finally found her voice and yelled for Dain to jump off. She was almost happy to see him beginning to fall off the beetle's side, until Dain's unthinking reactions kicked in. [PARAGRAPH]Garon was right, even with his simple training Dain was already starting to use the spear as an extension of his arm. Reflexively Dain thrust the point of the spear down hard into the beetles back. The sharp steel point must have found a seam between the thick plates and the beetles reaction was immediate, it spun so fast its head and dangerous horn where readied for Dain before Dain hit the ground. Forgetting its digging the beetle charged toward Dain as he scrambled away. Unable to get to his feet fast enough Dain's mind raced through every spear lesson Garon had given him. For the first time he wished he had paid closer attention. [PARAGRAPH]He remembered enough to set the butt of his spear in the ground, putting his weight on it as he readied the point against the charging beetle. Unconcerned with the spear the beetle lowered its head and hit it full force. For a brief second everything stopped, then the spear splintered loudly. The spear cut a deep gouge in the hard shell that covered the beetle's forehead and a trickle of syrupy blood could be seen from the wound. But now Dain lay prostrate before the beetle as it tried to figure out what had happened and what to do next. [PARAGRAPH]The decision was made for it. Kirien screamed so loud the lazy beetle, who had ignored everything up to this point, finally took notice and began lumbering slowly away. Kirien also hurled a fist sized stone at the beetle that stood over Dain, striking it in the side of its giant onyx face. [PARAGRAPH]The beetle turned and charged Kirien. Without a spear Kirien dived behind the only cover she could find, the torn up tree the beetle had already wrecked. Confused and in pain the beetle slammed into the tree. Its horn stuck the exposed inner soft wood and with an incredible show of strength it lifted its head and tore the small tree out of the ground. The tree fell first on the beetles back, who used the same shake it had used on Dain to throw it off on one side. The trees upper branches landed squarely on Dain, and Kirien quickly dove into the tangle of branches. [PARAGRAPH]Turning to examine the toppled tree the beetle looked around for any sign of movement. Kirien held perfectly still, and with the trees weight on top of him Dain had no choice but to do the same. The only movement the angry beetle spotted was the slowly fleeing form of the other beetle. It nudged the fallen tree one last time, then satisfied it had won its battle, fell in behind its companion. [PARAGRAPH]With Kirien's help Dain managed to crawl out from beneath the tree and they both collapsed on the ground without speaking. Despite the terrifying encounter it was only a few minutes before Dain finally spoke up, "I didn't need your help, I had everything under control. "[PARAGRAPH]"I wasn't trying to save you, I just really hate trees" she answered and they both laughed. [PARAGRAPH]After being so scared, laughing felt good and they continued to make jokes as they got up and checked the damage the falling tree had left on Dain. His left shoulder was bruised from the fall from the beetles back and he had dozens of scratches on his face and arms from the tree. Fortunately Dain's clothes were in good shape, he had got in so much trouble when the tower door had singed them, but a foot and a half of splintered wood was all that remained of the spear. Dain used that to poke at where the beetle had been digging. [PARAGRAPH]"What is it?" Kirien asked, peering over his shoulder. [PARAGRAPH]Dain used the sharp edge of the stick to dig into the dirt, exposing a dark green root. [PARAGRAPH]"This isn't a part of the tree, I've never seen anything like it. " he said yanking it out of the ground. He dusted the remaining dirt off of it as they examined it, both disappointed that their treasure looked to little more than an odd potato. [PARAGRAPH]"It stinks. " Kirien explained backing away from Dain. Dain sniffed at it and wrinkled his nose in disgust. [PARAGRAPH]"You're right, but after fighting for it I'm not leaving it behind. " Dain shoved the root in his pocket and asked, "So, what's next?"[PARAGRAPH]CHAPTER 2: LIVANNA[PARAGRAPH]A few hours later Dain and Kirien were walking back towards Brigdarrow sharing increasingly exaggerated stories of the beetle battle. Dain described the treasure he wished they'd found, a chest overflowing with coins and a gleaming steel sword. [PARAGRAPH]"You mean like that?" Kirien said pointing toward a silver glint in the long yellow grass. [PARAGRAPH]Dain squinted, but even in the fading light he could see the bright metal shape in the grass ahead. And this wasn't like the dull grey metal of Dain's former spear point or the worn copper coins the peddlers used to buy wheat and sell farm tools and supplies. It looked like polished silver. [PARAGRAPH]As they walker closer Dain was already speculating about what it was. A knight's shield, a scale from a dragon, and all manner of even more unlikely things. But none of his guesses had been close. [PARAGRAPH]"It's a dog. " Kirien said as if it seemed so unlikely that she was trying to convince herself of what she was seeing by saying it out loud. [PARAGRAPH]And it was a dog. Not an unusually sized one, with its head coming up to just above Dain's waist if it stood up. But it wasn't standing, it was laying on its side straining to take shallow, ragged breaths. There was a deep gash in its side and thick reddish brown blood matted its metallic silver hair. [PARAGRAPH]This time it was Kirien who acted to impulsively and she reached for the injured animal. The dog snarled and bit at her with surprising speed, hobbling up on three legs before collapsing again. She stepped back, more concerned for the dog than for her own safety. [PARAGRAPH]"What hurt it?" Dain asked, looking around and not seeing anything more dangerous than a few crows in the sky. [PARAGRAPH]"I don't know. "[PARAGRAPH]The dog's ears turned toward their voices. It turned its head toward Kirien, as if it was trying to recognize her, but its vision was dimmed by pain and exhaustion. Kirien reached for the dog but she backed off after receiving another growl. [PARAGRAPH]"We need to get Auric. " Dain said. "He would be able to get close to her, and would know how to treat those wounds. "[PARAGRAPH]"We can't leave her. She could die out here, especially if whatever hurt her comes back. "[PARAGRAPH]"If whatever hurt her comes back, we don't want to be here. " Dain said looking at the long cut in the animal's side. "That isn't a bite wound. "[PARAGRAPH]"Maybe it was another beetle?" Kirien offered, but she didn't sound convinced. [PARAGRAPH]"Maybe. "[PARAGRAPH]"If we wait until she's unconscious we could treat the wound. " Kirien suggested. [PARAGRAPH]"With what, we don't know anything more than putting some clean wraps on it, which we don't have. We have to get Auric, and neither one of us is staying out here alone after dark. " Dain was unaccustomed to being the voice of reason, but almost dying once in a day was enough, even for him. [PARAGRAPH]"We are about twenty minutes from the village, it will probably take longer than that for her to fall unconscious. I can find my way back here. Let's go get Auric. "[PARAGRAPH]Kirien reluctantly agreed, she told the dog to rest and promised they would return quickly. Then they took off jogging to Brigdarrow. [PARAGRAPH]CHAPTER 3: AURIC[PARAGRAPH]Auric Ulvin was the only boy in the village exempted from weapons practice. He was 16 and most of the village thought he was cursed. He could often be found around the village, his brown hair refusing to obey any straightening or gravity. His clothes, no matter how carefully tailored, always looked to be too small or too large for him. He rarely slept, sometimes going over a week without it. But Auric's quiet demeanor and likeable, never offensive, nature changed him from would have been a village pariah to a bit of local color. And people were frequently amazed at how much he knew about obscure topics, what plants will make a sore stomach go away, what the different star clusters are supposed to mean, how lake frogs seem to grow forever when away from the lake but never get much past cat sized if they stay. [PARAGRAPH]It was almost dusk when Dain and Kirien arrived at Ulvin Farm. It was late autumn and the farm, which had been surrounded by orderly rows of wheat for the past few months, was now surrounded by bare land and dust. Tawny went to knock on the closed shutters of Auric's window but Dain stopped her and pulled her toward the barn instead. [PARAGRAPH]After opening the barn door enough to squeeze inside Dain called out into the darkness for Auric. Long haired cows chewed their dinner while staring at visitors. Goats ignored the confines of their pens and only stopped briefly to check out the pair before returning to their climbing and play fights. [PARAGRAPH]Dain called out for Auric again and this time they heard movement in the barn's loft. [PARAGRAPH]"There is a hurt dog out past the tower" Dain answered, "can you come look at her?"[PARAGRAPH]"Tomorrow. " Auric said rolling back out of sight. [PARAGRAPH]Kirien spotted a ladder leading up into the loft and climbed up. Auric lay on a blanket in the hay looking typically disheveled, but even in the dim light of the loft Kirien could tell he was more exhausted than normal. [PARAGRAPH]"Are you okay?" she asked. [PARAGRAPH]"I'm fine," he said unconvincingly, "I'm just tired. "[PARAGRAPH]Kirien was about to give up, but Dain came up into the loft behind her and started explaining how hurt the dog was and how she could die before morning. He continued until Auric grudgingly agreed to go look at her. [PARAGRAPH]A few minutes later, after Auric picked up a small satchel full of clean bandages and herbs, the three were off across the plains. The dog hadn't moved, and her breathing was growing more difficult. She was too weak to bite as Auric examined her, and just bared her teeth in silent warning. [PARAGRAPH]"She's lost a lot of blood. " Auric said rooting through his satchel and laying out bandages and an ointment that smelled like rotten cabbage. [PARAGRAPH]Kirien tentatively petted the dogs head, then when the dog stopped snarling Kirien put the dogs head on her lap and held her so he wouldn't turn and bite Auric. Both of the boys ignored her. Auric began applying the bandages and Dain was staring wide-eyed at the wound. [PARAGRAPH]Kirien's grip on the head was unnecessary as Livanna lay helplessly and allowed Auric to bandage her. Livanna didn't react, except to whine painfully when she was lifted to wrap the bandages around her body. [PARAGRAPH]"Can we take her back to your farm?" Dain asked. [PARAGRAPH]"No," Auric said, "she shouldn't be moved. I'll sleep out here tonight, you two should go back to the village. I think she will be okay. "[PARAGRAPH]Kirien bent down and kissed the dog's forehead. Then she and Dain started the walk back to Brigdarrow. [PARAGRAPH]CHAPTER 4: GOSEA[PARAGRAPH]Dain expected to get in trouble when he returned to the village. But he hadn't expected search parties to be out looking for him. As they neared Brigdarrow they spotted a group with lantern's out by Tarch's Tower waving their lights around and calling for them. Both Dain and Kirien called back and went running toward the group. [PARAGRAPH]While Dain and Kirien were gone travelers passed through the village. A woman with skin like moonlight and two escorts dressed in horse-hair cloaks, worn leather armor and thick, thirsty axes. One had a single double-bladed axe and the other a pair of twin hand axes. It was unusual to see strangers in the remote village, but they were free with their coins so the village welcomed them. It wasn't until Jerra realized Dain and Kirien were missing that the village grew suspicious, and although sneaking off wasn't uncommon for the pair, they had never been gone so late before. Concerns quickly grew to fear and now most of the village was out looking for them. [PARAGRAPH]Within the village the three strangers were being questioned by Thegn Garon Ire and a group of villagers, including Dain's father, who watched suspiciously as the three repeated their claims of innocence. Both of the men being accused stood protectively beside the unarmed woman, who looked to be the only calm one in the group. [PARAGRAPH]"Dad!" Dain yelled as he ran toward them. [PARAGRAPH]At his voice the group broke and although no one had drawn their weapons, muscles relaxed and hands resting dangerously close to hilts moved away. A flicker of relief flashed across Havis's face at the sight of his son, then disappeared quickly, replaced by anger. Dain's run faltered and he considered running back out to spend the night with Auric before realizing that he may deserve that anger. [PARAGRAPH]"Is Kirien okay?" Garon asked. [PARAGRAPH]"Yes, she is with her mother. We were just out exploring. " Dain answered. [PARAGRAPH]"What happened?" Garon said noticing the broken spear shaft in Dain's hand. [PARAGRAPH]Dain considered telling them about the dog with the silver fur, but the strange woman made him nervous. She seemed equally interested in his story, and her dark eyes were beautiful, but they were also cold. The wound in Livanna's side could have been made by her escort's axes, so Dain didn't say anything about the dog. [PARAGRAPH]"Nothing, we were just too far away when it started to get late. I'm sorry. "[PARAGRAPH]Left with the realization that their entire confrontation had been for nothing the group fell into an uncomfortable silence until the strange woman spoke. [PARAGRAPH]"Thegn, may I have the items you confiscated?"[PARAGRAPH]"Of course," Garon replied awkwardly, "I apologize for our alarm. There was a lecture on the way home, a whipping before bed and he was told he was going to spend the next day with Father Prespin, the villages doddering priest of Danalin. [PARAGRAPH]Dain was sure Kirien wasn't being punished as severely. Although his father avoided launching into another lecture Dain could tell that he was close to doing it. So Dain stayed quiet and did as he was told. [PARAGRAPH]Just after dawn Dain's father walked him to the small village temple to Danalin, god of water. Father Prespin was already prepared and greeted the two at the door. [PARAGRAPH]"Come in, come in, I just put on some tea. "[PARAGRAPH]Havis declined the offer, stating that he was a day behind because of the prior day's chaos. [PARAGRAPH]"Many people think the gods are there to help us, that they will protect us from bad things. " Prespin said as he sat down and offered a cup of tea to Dain. [PARAGRAPH]Dain's butt wasn't quite ready for sitting so he stood as he sipped his tea. [PARAGRAPH]"No father", Dain answered, "I don't think he would. "[PARAGRAPH]"So we must protect ourselves, and each other. We will not know when danger comes for us. "[PARAGRAPH]"Yes father", Dain answered dutifully. [PARAGRAPH]Dain spent the rest of the morning cleaning the temple and talking with Father Prespin. [PARAGRAPH]Dain slid up beside Kirien and hooked his bucket up to the well rope. [PARAGRAPH]"Have you heard anything from Auric?" he whispered. [PARAGRAPH]"I went and saw him and Livanna this morning. Livanna looks much better. I took her some food and water and she gobbled it up. "[PARAGRAPH]"You left the village this morning?" "[PARAGRAPH]"That sounds horrible," Dain replied, rolling his eyes. [PARAGRAPH]Kirien ignored him. [PARAGRAPH]"That strange woman and her two guards left the village early this morning. [PARAGRAPH]"No, I don't trust her. "[PARAGRAPH]"Me either. " Then after a pause Dain added. "Do you think they attacked Livanna?"[PARAGRAPH]"I don't know," Kirien said. "But I'm glad they're gone. [PARAGRAPH]CHAPTER 6: LYRR[PARAGRAPH]Dain wasn't able to slip away again until the following day. Dain's father decided that as irresponsible as Dain was, he was much worse when Kirien was around.
